methods.label: Compare the conditional forms
methods.explanation:
Use the intended schematic reading: let \(P\) denote the angle-equality condition and \(Q\) the isosceles condition, treating “not equal” in statements 1 and 3 as the negation of \(P\). The given theorem has the form \(P\Rightarrow Q\). We are comparing conditional forms, without adding other triangle theorems.

Statement 3 has the form \(\neg Q\Rightarrow\neg P\). This is the contrapositive. Both it and the original implication fail in exactly the same situation: \(P\) is true and \(Q\) is false. They are therefore logically equivalent.

Statement 4 says that \(Q\) is necessary for \(P\). This means that \(P\) cannot hold without \(Q\), which is precisely \(P\Rightarrow Q\).

Statements 1 and 2 have the inverse and converse forms, \(\neg P\Rightarrow\neg Q\) and \(Q\Rightarrow P\). Neither is equivalent to the original conditional form: when \(P\) is false and \(Q\) is true, the original implication is true but both of these forms are false. A converse can happen to be a true geometry theorem without being logically equivalent in form to the original implication.

Thus the required statements are \(3\) and \(4\), choice E.
